elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence covers only professional liability (E&O) and cyber/privacy liability; there is no commercial general liability covenant anywhere in the rendered text (5.3 remains permissive: "Any of the Parties may at its own expense insure against risks"). Defect: no operative CGL per-occurrence limit of USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No aggregate CGL limit appears in the insertion or elsewhere. Defect: no operative CGL aggregate limit of USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Insertion sets E&O at "not less than USD 1,000,000", which is the fallback figure and below the preferred USD 2,000,000. Defect: raise the E&O limit to USD 2,000,000 for the preferred level.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Insertion sets cyber and privacy liability at "not less than USD 2,000,000", below the preferred USD 5,000,000; no Customer Data processing trigger is drafted. Defect: increase cyber/privacy limit to USD 5,000,000 (covering all data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer) for the preferred level.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation obligation is present in the insertion or in retained 5.3 / the cost definition. Defect: add a statutory workers' compensation covenant.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: No certificate mechanic exists; the comment acknowledges the certificate mechanic "remain[s] available" but it is not in operative language. Defect: add an obligation to furnish certificates of insurance on request.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative sentence: "Each Party other than Teleglobe USA Inc. shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000..." — mandatory "shall", correct coverage type, correct floor, imposed on the counterparties.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence: "...and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000." Coverage type and amount match the fallback exactly.

reasons: Finding kind is correctly characterised as missing: the document contains no mandatory insurance covenant — 5.3 is permissive ("may at its own expense insure") and the cost definition expressly contemplates "a reasonable allowance in lieu of insurance if such Party elects to carry a risk itself", so no insurance element was previously met.

Fallback is position-complete: a single mandatory sentence carries both fallback elements at the exact required coverage types and floors (E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber and privacy USD 2,000,000), with correct party direction (obligation on the counterparties, not on us).

Preferred is not complete: CGL 1M/2M, E&O at 2M, cyber at 5M, workers' compensation and the certificate mechanic are all absent from operative language; the comment's reference to those limits remaining "available" is a promise, not a term.

Minimality holds: nothing is deleted or paraphrased, favourable existing language (5.3 and the cost allocation definitions) is retained, and the insertion carries no model-language extras — no "at its own expense", no survival tail, no certificate or notice procedure, no additional coverage lines beyond the two fallback elements. Carving out our own entity is a party-direction limitation rather than an added requirement, so it does not offend minimality.

Intent is preserved: the insertion is a free-standing covenant that does not disturb the Capital Cost mechanics, Management Committee approval, or the self-insurance allowance in the cost definition, and leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference. Retained 5.3 addresses optional insurance of a Party's own share of Capital Costs — a different subject from mandatory E&O and cyber cover — so it is a tension worth noting rather than a contradictory retained sentence; if counterparties argue 5.3 makes all insurance optional, add "Notwithstanding paragraph 5.3," to the insertion.

Drafting note for the negotiation record: the insertion has no temporal anchor (no "throughout the term"); the fallback checklist does not require one, so this is a rationale-level observation, not a deviation.
